vicptpatronage

An R package and Shiny app for exploring how Victorian public transport patronage has recovered since the COVID-19 pandemic, and whether Victoria’s 2025-2026 free-travel and half-price fare periods left a lasting boost.

Website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-pian0dan/

Who this is for

Built for a Victorian transport policy analyst or journalist asking: how has each public transport mode’s patronage recovered relative to its pre-pandemic baseline, and did recent fare discounts produce a lasting change or just a temporary bump?

Data

vicptpatronage bundles monthly_patronage: monthly patron boardings for six Victorian public transport modes (metropolitan train, tram and bus; V/Line regional train, coach and bus) from January 2018 onward.

  • Source: Victorian Department of Transport and Planning, Open Data portal, “Monthly public transport patronage by mode”, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0.
  • Mode icons: the Department’s official Transport Pictograms dataset, also CC BY 4.0.
  • One data-quality issue was found and corrected during preparation (a corrupted cell in the raw “Regional bus” column), and a fare_period column flags months affected by fare discounts, with sources for each date range documented in data-raw/monthly_patronage.R and ?monthly_patronage.

Installation

Not on CRAN; install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-pian0dan")

Launching the app 

library(vicptpatronage)
run_app()

See vignette("vicptpatronage") for a full walkthrough of the data, the patronage_index() function, and how to use and interpret the app.

Generative AI declaration

I used Posit Assistant (built on Claude, via Posit AI Pass in Positron) throughout the development of this assignment, for:

  • scaffolding the R package structure (DESCRIPTION, data-raw/, inst/app/, roxygen documentation, pkgdown configuration);
  • writing and iterating on the data cleaning script, including identifying and resolving a corrupted value in the source CSV;
  • building and substantially revising the Shiny app, including diagnosing and fixing several plotly/ggplotly integration issues (e.g. invisible background shading, a malformed legend, and low-contrast hover text);
  • researching and sourcing the app’s colour palette and icons from official Public Transport Victoria assets, and verifying fare-discount dates against official government sources;
  • correcting a methodological issue in the patronage indexing approach (an unaddressed seasonality confound, and later an overstated free-travel period that didn’t distinguish weekend-only from every-day free travel);
  • refactoring app code into the package’s R/ directory as internal functions, instead of loose script-level code;
  • drafting this README, the package vignette, and _pkgdown.yml.

I reviewed, tested, and revised all generated code and text, ran devtools::check() throughout to verify correctness, and take full responsibility for the content of this submission.
